name: Quest Book
subtitle: The pack’s own guided progression, chapter by chapter

text.v: The quest book is the modpack’s hand-written guide. Each chapter below lists its quests in book order, with the tasks you must complete and the rewards you get.

entries.text:
Chapter 2: Allthemodium
Allthemodium
Obviously now that you are in Chapter 2, you have beaten Vanilla Minecraft!
By now you should have Netherite and have killed all the bosses Minecraft has. So what's next?
Allthemodium is what's next! In order to start getting Allthemodium though you will need Netherite. Let's start there!
Tasks: Netherite IngotRewards: Guide Book
Teleport Pad
For 4 Allthemodium Nuggets and an Ender Pearl you get a Teleport Pad.
Place it down in one of the Minecraft dimensions to teleport to a different dimension.
To teleport you need to shift right click with your main and offhand empty! That is important, read it!
BOTH hands need to be EMPTY!
Tasks: Teleport PadRewards: Allthemodium Nugget ×4
Mining Dimension
The Mining Dimension is a Superflat world with absolutely nothing on the surface.
Below the surface is almost every single Ore.
The Mining Dimension has no Caves, no Mob Spawns, and nothing to get in your way. It's just Stone types and Ores!
Ore spawns differ for the Y Level and layer in the Mining Dimension.
I recommend setting up a Quarry.
Tasks: Visit ATM Mining DimRewards: Enchanted Book
The Other
The Other has seen dozens of changes over the years but always it has been a realm for adventures!
There's dozens of new biomes, blocks, and of course structures!
The Structures are: Piglin Village, Ancient Pyramid, and Dungeon. All containing amazing loot with some things being unique to their structure!
You can also mine for Vibranium (and other ores!) or find it and better in the structures!
You can't set up Quarries or many blocks in The Other though, no cheesing anything here.
Tasks: Visit The OtherRewards: Potion
The Beyond
Welcome to The Beyond!
There's nothing here!
You might want an Angel Block.
Tasks: Visit The BeyondRewards: Angel Block
Ancient City
Only the hardest Structure in Vanilla Minecraft. So of course that's where you'll have to look for Allthemodium!
You can find the Ore in the walls of Caves around the Ancient Cities, it's Glowing so it'll be easy to spot just very rare!
Tasks: StructureRewards: White Wool ×64
Allthemodium Ingot
To mine Allthemodium you'll need a Pickaxe that is Netherite Tier or higher!
Once you finally get the Ore (first I recommend processing it either with Fortune, Occultism, or Mekanism to get more) then you can get a few choices of what to do with it.
I recommend making 2 Teleport Pads with the Nuggets! You can use those to get to the Mining Dimension to find more Allthemodium or The Other to find other adventures.
After that I recommend upgrading your Pickaxe so you can Mine Vibranium. The rest is all up to you!
Tasks: Allthemodium IngotRewards: Allthemodium Ingot 500 XP
Allthemodium Smithing Template
Another Item you can only find in Ancient Cities is the Allthemodium Smithing Template.
To get it you'll need to Brush suspicious Clay.
You can find it in the floors of the Ancient City.
Tasks: AllTheModium Smithing TemplateRewards: AllTheModium Smithing Template
Vibranium Smithing Template
To upgrade Allthemodium to Vibranium you will need another Smithing Template. This one you can find by Brushing Suspicious Soul Sand.
Which is found in Bastions in The Nether.
Tasks: Vibranium Smithing TemplateRewards: Vibranium Smithing Template
Allthemodium Armor
Direct upgrade from Netherite.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Allthemodium Ingot
Smart Filter
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Allthemodium Ingot
Allthemodium Tools
Can't craft these anymore now you need to upgrade Netherite to it always. Yes, it saves Enchantments and Repairs it!
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Allthemodium Ingot
Allthemodium Bow
Tasks: Allthemodium Bow
Allthemodium Mace
Vanilla couldn't all the fun with Maces! So of course there is an Allthemodium upgrade to them!
Upgrade a Mace with an Allthemodium Block to get the Allthemodium Mace.
It does more base damage, more falling damage, and same Enchantments!
Tasks: Allthemodium MaceRewards: Allthemodium Ingot
Unobtainium Armor
Best basic Armor you can get!
Will be needed to craft the Mekasuit which is better though!
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Unobtainium Ingot
Allthemodium Spell Book
Tasks: Allthemodium Spell Book
Smart Filter
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Unobtainium Ingot
Unobtainium Spell Book
Tasks: Unobtainium Spell Book
Unobtainium Tools
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Unobtainium Ingot
Unobtainium Crossbow
Tasks: Unobtainium Crossbow
Unobtainium Mace
Tasks: Unobtainium MaceRewards: Unobtainium Ingot
Vibranium Armor
Direct upgrade to Allthemodium.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Vibranium Ingot
Smart Filter
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Vibranium Ingot
Vibranium Tools
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Vibranium Ingot
Vibranium Shield
Tasks: Vibranium Shield
Vibranium Mace
Tasks: Vibranium MaceRewards: Vibranium Ingot
Vibranium Spell Book
Tasks: Vibranium Spell Book
The Nether
Place the Teleport Pad in The Nether to go to The Other.
Tasks: Visit The NetherRewards: Potion
Overworld
Place the Teleport Pad in the Overworld to go to the Mining Dimension.
Tasks: Visit Overworld
The End
Place the Teleport Pad in The End to go to The Beyond.
Tasks: Visit The EndRewards: Potion
Vibranium Ingot
Vibranium is the next ore after Allthemodium, so of course it requires Allthemodium Pickaxe (or the same tier) to mine it.
You can find it rarely in The Nether or abundantly in The Other.
It is also recommend to Ore Process it to get more.
Sadly, while it's a cool colored ATM ore, it has the least uses for different Items.
Tasks: Vibranium IngotRewards: Vibranium Ingot 500 XP
Unobtainium Smithing Template
Another Smithing Template?!?!?!
Well atleast you don't need Archeology for it!
You'll have to earn these by beating the Trial Spawners which are found in the Dungeon structure in The Other. More specifically the Library Rooms!
Tasks: Unobtainium Smithing TemplateRewards: Unobtainium Smithing Template
Unobtainium Ingot
No it isn't found in The Beyond.
You can find Unobtainium Ore very rarely in End Highlands Biomes. Those are usually where End Cities spawn as well!
You'll need a Vibranium Pickaxe (or same Tier) to Mine the Ore.
Do I need to still tell you to Ore process it?
Tasks: Unobtainium IngotRewards: Unobtainium Ingot 500 XP
Quest
To combine Vibranium, Unobtainium, and Allthemodium we'll need to venture into Powah!
Place the Energizing Orb down then put Energizing Rods facing it. The Energizing Rods need to be placed on a Power Source and will send Energy into the Orb. The amount each holds and sends is determined by the Tier.
Place the Ingots, 2 Piglich Hearts, and a Compressed Block of Nitro Crystals X1 into the Orb (order doesn't matter). Then once 1 Billion FE is put into the Orb through the Rods it'll be ready!
{ "text": "POWAH QUESTLINE", "color": "#55FF55", "underlined": true, "clickEvent": { "action": "change_page", "value": "2A6EBEEBAB882679" } }
Tasks: Energizing OrbRewards: Random loot roll
Unobtainium - Allthemodium Alloy Ingot
Unobtainium combined with Allthemodium!
Tasks: Unobtainium - Allthemodium Alloy IngotRewards: Unobtainium Ingot ×3 Allthemodium Ingot ×3
Unobtainium - Vibranium Alloy Ingot
Vibranium combined with Unobtainium!
Tasks: Unobtainium - Vibranium Alloy IngotRewards: Vibranium Ingot ×3 Unobtainium Ingot ×3
Vibranium - Allthemodium Alloy Ingot
Vibranium combined with Allthemodium!
Tasks: Vibranium - Allthemodium Alloy IngotRewards: Vibranium Ingot ×3 Allthemodium Ingot ×3
Piglich Boss
The Piglich is a Boss added by Allthemodium.
Has he 1000 Hearts and currently has no attacks but trust me when he does they will be devastating!
When killed he'll drop his Heart which will be needed for Alloys and the ATM Star!
(Look into ways of farming them like with HNN or EnderIO!)
Tasks: Piglich HeartRewards: Piglich Heart
Ancient Pyramid
The Ancient Pyramid is one of the 3 Structures in The Other.
Clearly it is a Pyramid and no this one doesn't have a basement!
Instead it has the Piglich.
Tasks: StructureRewards: Golden Apple ×32
Allthemodium Alloy Paxel
Only the greatest Tool in history! Like a swiss army knife but better!
Highest Mining Tier, chops down Trees like butter, makes pathways, and of course hits a lot to be hit by!
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy PaxelRewards: Enchanted Book Block of Unobtainium - Allthemodium Alloy Block of Unobtainium - Vibranium Alloy Block of Vibranium - Allthemodium Alloy 5000 XP
Allthemodium Alloy Axe
Does a ton of damage, and chops down trees! What more do you need?
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy AxeRewards: Enchanted Book 1000 XP
Allthemodium Alloy Shovel
Yes it can make pathways don't worry!
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy ShovelRewards: Enchanted Book 1000 XP
Allthemodium Alloy Pick
A very fast pickaxe.
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy PickRewards: Enchanted Book 1000 XP
Allthemodium Alloy Sword
Second in damage of all Swords. The first in damage does Infinite, and there's no competing with Infinite.
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy BladeRewards: Enchanted Book 1000 XP
Allthemodium Alloy Trident
Tasks: Allthemodium Alloy Trident
Quest

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

entries.text:
Chapter 1: The Beginning
Welcome to Getting Started!
ATM10 is a Kitchensink pack, meaning you are free to explore and play the modpack any way that you want!
However, there is an endgame goal: Making the ATM Star!
This questline serves as a guide for all players, whether you are brand new to Minecraft or you've played through previous ATM packs.
Just like almost every modpack, gather some wood to get started!
Tasks: Any LogsRewards: Torch ×4 Cooked Beef ×4
Putting the Craft in Minecraft
I'm going to assume you've been crafting, right? It is MineCRAFT after all.
Sure, you could craft in your inventory using the 2x2 crafting grid, but that won't get you far. We need to upgrade by making a Crafting Table!
Tasks: Crafting TableRewards: 10 XP
Our First Pick
Whether you are an experienced modded player, or a complete noob to MC, everyone has to make a Wooden Pickaxe.
Pickaxes allow you to break most stone and metal blocks. This wooden one won't last long, so make sure to gather some Cobblestone with it!
Tasks: Wooden PickaxeRewards: Oak Log ×2 Random loot roll 10 XP
Crafting, but on a Stick
Personally, I hate having to run to a block just to craft. That's where the Crafting Table on a Stick comes in!
This item works as a Portable Crafting Table!
Tip: You can also put this in your Curios slot and set a Keybind to open it!
Tasks: %1$s%2$s%3$sRewards: 10 XP
Stone Age
With our Wooden Pickaxe, stone shouldn't be a problem to break!
Cobblestone unlocks the next part of the progression by using it to craft a Furnace to smelt our ores.
You'll also want to upgrade your pickaxe to stone to mine better ores like Iron!
Tasks: Any Cobblestones ×16 FurnaceRewards: 10 XP
Furnace Upgrades!
With our new metals, we can upgrade our Furnace using the mod Iron Furnaces!
Iron Furnaces (Furnaces from the mod itself, not just the Iron version) allow you to add Augments to upgrade its speed, change the function of the furnace, and more!
These furnaces make automation easier by allowing you to auto-pull or push from the sides using the config on the left of the interface.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: 10 XP
The Metal Age
I'm going to assume you've been out mining, right? It is MINEcraft after all.
You'll find a ton of new ores that might confuse you, but you can stick to the vanilla materials to get you started!
Copper is abundant and has plenty of uses for things like Ore Hammers or Drawer Upgrades, so make sure to grab plenty of it!
Iron is probably one of the most important ores you'll want to get every time you run into it. The world of modded MC pretty much runs on Iron.
Tasks: Iron Ingot Copper IngotRewards: Loot 25 XP
An Iron Pick
The next step of progression is to make an Iron Pickaxe.
This pickaxe can mine some of the rarer ores in the game, including Diamond!
Tasks: Iron PickaxeRewards: 50 XP
Redstone
Once you have an Iron or better tier Pickaxe, you'll be able to mine Redstone.
Redstone starts your journey into many technical mods, like creating power or making fancy gadgets.
This is a resource you will want a lot of!
Tasks: Redstone ×4Rewards: 25 XP
We've Struck Diamonds!
Diamonds are one of the best materials to use for tool crafting, but also allows you to visit new dimensions like the Nether!
Tasks: DiamondRewards: Loot 50 XP
To The Nether!
With a Diamond tier pickaxe, you'll be able to mine Obsidian. Obsidian can be used to create a portal to the Nether.
The portal frame can be many different sizes, but most go with the basic 'Door' shape. This is a hollow 4x5 shape using a minimum of 10 Obsidian. You don't have to use Obsidian for the corners, just the portal frame itself!
Tasks: Obsidian ×10 Advancement: minecraft:story/enter_the_netherRewards: Golden Chestplate 50 XP
Basic Ore Doubling
Smelting down raw ores in the beginning is necessary, but you are missing out on extra resources!
There are several ways to double your output per raw ore, but one of the easiest ways is by creating and using an Ore Hammer.
These will break down 1 raw ore into 2 dusts which can be smelting into ingots, effectively doubling your ingot output!
Want more per raw ore? Check out the mod Occultism!
Tasks: Any Ore HammersRewards: Iron Dust ×3 Copper Dust ×3 25 XP
Smart Filter
There are many ways to store power!
Powah offers great storage using Energy Cells that can be upgraded, or you can always go with the multiblock style of RFTools using Powercells! The choice is yours.
Note: You only have to make one of the items to complete the quest.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Advanced Universal Cable ×3 50 XP
Smart Filter
Transferring power out of your generators is probably a good idea, but how can you do it?
To start, you can use cables from Mekanism, or you can use the Powah Energy Cables if you have already started using that mod.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Redstone Block 50 XP
Finding The End
Once you've gathered enough Ender Pearls and Blaze Powders, you can make your way to the End Portal in the Overworld.
To do this, craft some Eyes of Ender and right click to throw them in the sky. These will point in the direction of the closest End Portal.
Make your way to the Stronghold, find the End Portal, and complete the frame using the Eyes of Ender to create the portal to The End.
Tasks: Ender Eye ×10 Advancement: minecraft:story/follow_ender_eyeRewards: Ender Pearl ×4 Random loot roll
The End
In The End, you'll find the final boss of Vanilla Minecraft: The Ender Dragon.
At the top of each pillar of Obsidian, you'll find an End Crystal that heals the Dragon. Make sure to take those out first! They also do a lot of damage, so make sure to create some distance!
Once defeated, a Dragon Egg spawns at the top of the Exit Portal. This cannot be mined like normal blocks, but is affected by gravity.
Tasks: Advancement: minecraft:end/dragon_eggRewards: 250 XP
Gearing Up
This quest only requires you to make one Diamond tool or armor piece, but it's probably good to get a full set!
Diamond tools boast high durability, and the armor offers great protection overall.
To make the better tools and armor in the game, you'll need Diamond stuff as a base!
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Diamond ×2 50 XP
Netherite Template
To create Netherite tools and armor you'll need to find the Netherite Smithing Template in chests found inside of Bastions.
These can be combined with a Netherite ingot and a Diamond tool or armor in a Smithing Table to upgrade it to Netherite.
Tip: Don't use all of your templates in one go! You can create duplicates by using the recipe to create another.
Tasks: Netherite Upgrade Smithing TemplateRewards: Netherite Upgrade Smithing Template 100 XP
Netherite Tier
Netherite items are even better overall, and won't burn in lava! You still will though, even wearing the armor. Don't try it out.
This items can be used to make some of the best tools and armor in the game.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Diamond ×3 50 XP
Archaeology!
Achaeology allows players to find items inside of Suspicious blocks like Sand and Gravel.
These blocks can be found in various structures like Warm Ocean Ruins, Desert Pyramids, Desert Wells, and Trail Ruins.
To uncover an item from a Suspicious block, you need to create a Brush to brush away the block to unveil an item.
Tasks: BrushRewards: Brush 50 XP
Ancient Metals
In the Nether, you'll run into Ancient Debris. This can be smelted down into Scraps that can be combined with Gold to create Netherite Ingots, which is an endgame metal use to craft some of the strongest tools and armor in the game.
Tasks: Netherite IngotRewards: Netherite Scrap ×3 100 XP
Visit The Deep Dark!
This biome was introduced in the Wild Update!
Be careful! You might accidentally summon a new friend.
P.S. - He's not friendly.
Tasks: BiomeRewards: 50 XP
Armor Trims
Armor Trims are items used to add trims to your armor! This can be done in Smithing Tables.
While they do have a recipe, most of the trims are rare finds in from loot chests or archaeology digs. Once you find one, you can dupe the Template by using the recipe to create more!
Tasks: Any Trim TemplatesRewards: 100 XP
The Sniffer
Scruff McGruff's Distant Cousin
To find this egg, you'll need to brush away Suspicious Sand in Warm Ocean Ruins.
You can place the Egg into the world and it will slowly hatch into a Snifflet. This takes around 20 minutes to hatch normally, but can be placed on a Moss block to double the hatch speed, taking only 10 minutes to hatch.
The Snifflet will eventually grow into an adult Sniffer that can sniff up items like Torchflower Seeds or Pitcher Pods when they wander over blocks they can dig in.
You can breed 2 adult Sniffers by using Torchflowers.
Tasks: Sniffer EggRewards: Brush 250 XP
Kill The Warden
The Warden can be summoned by setting off a Sculk Sensor that is near a Sculk Shrieker at least 3 times.
Fun Fact: The Warden is blind! It can only find you if it hears you, so either fly around or sneak!
Tip: It doesn't matter if you use Ranged or Melee attacks, because it will find you. And it will hit you. If you go too far, it'll burrow into the ground and come up next to you! Good luck :D
Tasks: Kill WardenRewards: 250 XP Potion
Kill The Wither
The Wither is one of the hardest bosses to kill in Minecraft. Mainly because it flies. And explodes. And is fast. You get the picture.
To summon it, place down the 4 Soul Sand in the shape of a T. Place the 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls on the top of the 'T' and the Wither will spawn.
Tip: It explodes. A lot. Don't do this near your base.
Tasks: Kill WitherRewards: 250 XP
Furnace Augments
Augments are Furnace upgrades that can either change or upgrade the function of a Furnace.
- Blasting: Converts the Furnace to only allow for Blasting recipes.
- Smoking: Converts the Furnace to only allow for Smoking recipes.
- Factory: Converts the Furnace to use power instead of fuel, and upgrades it to a factory, allowing it to smelt multiple items at once. This increases depending on the tier of Furnace.
- Speed: Doubles the speed of the furnace at the cost of double the fuel.
- Fuel Efficiency: Doubles the amount of items smelted per fuel, but reduces the speed by 25%
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: 10 XP
Summoning The Wither
To summon the boss of the Nether, we need to gather a few items first.
We'll need to get at least 3 Wither Skeleton Skulls. These are rare drops from killing Wither Skeletons, or can be crafted with the more common drop, the Wither Skull Fragments.
You'll also need at least 4 pieces of Soul Sand, and probably some pretty good armor.
Tasks: Wither Skeleton Skull ×3 Soul Sand ×4Rewards: Wither Skeleton Skull ×3
Wind Power
If you are like most this is the power you are after. All you do is place it as high as you can and get free power.
Tasks: Wind GeneratorRewards: Random loot roll
Solar Power
Just like wind generation this will give you lots of power without giving it any resources. The only downside here is it has to be daytime.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Random loot roll
Lava Power
Now that you have all this Lava what will you do with it? More early game power!
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Lava Bucket Crying Obsidian ×2 Obsidian ×6 Random loot roll
Smart Filter
Smelt your logs
Coal is your first real source of power. If you are running low and cant find any Coal a better alternative for you will be Charcoal.
Tasks: Any CoalsRewards: Oak Log ×6
Lava Bucket
Buckets and Tanks are a great early way to move around lava.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Iron Ingot

OreBerries
OreBerries can be made or found in world.
They are also compatable with the Harvester pylon, from Pylons, and their output has been buffed when using a pylon to automate them.
Tasks: Smart Filter Harvester Pylon

entries.text:
Relics
Relics
Welcome to Relics! Relics mod is similar to Artifacts, you get many unique and powerful items all throughout the Worlds. They have many different Abilities which are obtained and upgraded through the Research Window (Hold shift on the relic). There you can exchange Vanilla XP to reroll the stats on its abilites, see your current Relic XP, gained from using the Relics, and level up their abilities! To use Relic Abilities default is Left Alt.
Tasks: XpRewards: 2 XP levels
Reflecting Necklace
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
Pufferfish are pretty cool, same with Guardians, same with Thorns! Every damage dealt while wearing the Reflecting Necklace will accumulate points. Either after 5 seconds from last damage or when the points are full, the Necklace will shoot out Obsidian Spikes in all directions damaging all nearby.
Tasks: Reflecting NecklaceRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Magma Walkers
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
The Magma Walkers allow you 2 things, walking on Magma Blocks without taking damage, and walking on Lava for a little bit. Magma Blocks don't have a cooldown but walking on Lava does. After the period is over the Boots will overheat and damage you.
Tasks: Magma WalkerRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Magma Block ×10
Aqua Walkers
Found in Shipwrecks and Ocean Ruins
With Aqua Walkers you can use it's Ability to walk on Water! You can hold Shift to sink into Water and Swim. I think I've read about a story like that once?
Tasks: Aqua WalkerRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Water Bucket
Midnight Robe
Found in Mineshafts or Strongholds
Ever want to be just like Batman? Living in the shadows bringing justice? Then the Midnight Robe is perfect for you! {It's also stylish!) When worn in Low Light Levels you will become Invisible and be given Speed. This can be upgraded for the Light Levels to be higher or to give more Speed. The Second Ability gives remneants of most Stealth Games. When you hit a Mob while Invisible you'll deal much more damage but lose your stealth and speed until you leave the Circle made around the Mob.
Tasks: Midnight RobeRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Drowned Belt
Found in Shipwrecks and Ocean Ruins
First Ability with Drowned Belt is in the name, it's a Belt, it holds Talismans. The Second one works with swimming in the Water. Ever get jealous of how the Drowned move through the Water as if it were their home? Well with this Ability you can get similar! The Third one works like Impaling, you'll do increased Damage in the Water. And the Last Ability also works with Trident Enchanting, you can now use Channeling anywhere regardless of how wet!
Tasks: Drowned BeltRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Copper Ingot ×5
Jellyfish Necklace
Found in Shipwrecks and Ocean Ruins
Even though there might not be any Jellyfish in Minecraft we can get the power of them! With the Jellyfish Necklace! While wearing it, it's First and passive ability allows you to not sink in water, to walk over it. The Second Ability which is also a passive ability makes it so you sting mobs that come close to you. It can be upgraded to do more damage. The Last Ability grants an Effect to the Second Ability. Any mob hit with the Second Ability will be paralyzed! Kinda glad there isn't any Jellyfish in Minecraft now...
Tasks: Jellyfish NecklaceRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Hunter's Belt
Found in Butcher's Huts of any Village
The Hunter's Belt works like the Leather Belt as in it holds Talismans. That's its first ability which can be upgraded to hold more! The Second Ability increases the damage your pets do. Pets are tamed Mobs that can do damage to other Mobs, like wolves!
Tasks: Hunter BeltRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Bone ×10
Rage Glove
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
If you know the term 'Berserk' in most gaming, that will help you understand what the Rage Glove does. If you don't know, the basics of Berserk is when someone gets low health or takes lots of damage, usually they will deal higher damage and be faster. That's what happens with First Ability, when you take damage you accumulate points which can be exchanged for higher damage and speed! The Second Ability does that passively, and gives you Regeneration per the amount of health you lost. The Third Ability is an active one, when using it (Alt Tab) you will dash and attack any mob you are looking at. When hit it'll set them on Fire, give them Bleeding, and any accumulated Berserk points deal extra damage with it!
Tasks: Rage GloveRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Ice Skates
Found in Villages in Taigas or Snowy Taigas
Ever hate how slow Ice is unless using a Boat? Which still doesn't make sense to me! Ice Skates change that now you accelerate on Ice while wearing Ice Skates. You can upgrade them to accel faster! After upgrading them you can get a Second Ability which allows you to damage Mobs by running into them while wearing Ice Skates.
Tasks: Ice SkatesRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Ice ×10
Bastion Ring
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
The 'Babes' love the Bling! The Bastion Ring is perfect for the bartering man. While wearing it Piglins will be neutral with you like how they are when you wear Gold. This does not mean you can freely loot their chests though. The Ring will also give you a chance at getting more Loot from Bartering. (While wearing the Ring Piglins might point you toward the nearest Bastion).
Tasks: Bastion RingRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Gold Ingot ×10
Chorus Inhibitor
Found in End Cities and End Ships
Chorus Inhibitor is another simple Relic. It can teleport you to a block you are looking at if it's in range. The range can be upgraded in the Research Window.
Tasks: Chorus InhibitorRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Chorus Fruit ×10
Space Dissector
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
Space Dissector should named Wormhole Creator, it makes portals from one spot to another. To set the spots Hold Right Click to set the first portal, then move and stop Holding Right Click to set the second portal. You can upgrade them to increase the space between them and the time they are up. Hehe space and time, portals... if you were smarter you'd be laughing.
Tasks: Space DissectorRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Holy Locket
Found in all Villages
Okay this is a long one just stick with me. First Ability allows two modes, Sancity and Unholiness. Sancity takes some of your Healing and uses it as Damage against enemies. Unholiness does the opposite, it takes the enemies Healing to help you deal more damage. Mobs like Ender Dragon and Wither both regenerate Health. The Second Ability is Repentance, while active it will Burn Undead Mobs (Zombie, Skeleton, and their cousins). The Third Ability grants a small time period of Invincibility.
Tasks: Holy LocketRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Golden Apple
Ender Hand
Found in End Cities and End Ships
Ender Hand does two things a Passive Ability and an Active Ability. Passive makes Endermen not angry when you look at them. Active allows you to trade places with a mob you're looking at with Left Alt.
Tasks: Ender HandRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 End Stone ×10
Elytra Booster
Found in End Cities and End Ships
Are Rockets just too expensive? You can use an Elytra Booster instead of Rockets. Wear both Elytra and Elytra Booster, then Fuel the Booster. It accepts any Furnace Fuel: Coal, Lava, Logs, even Dried Kelp Blocks. Then when flying with an Elytra, Left Alt to press Accelerate! Now you're flying with much cheaper Eco-Friendly Fuel!
Tasks: Elytra BoosterRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Coal ×10
Magic Mirror
Found in Mineshafts or Strongholds
'Mirror Mirror on the wall how do I get back to my Respawn Point from my travels?' 'After setting the Magic Mirror to a Bed by right clicking with it, you can hold right click for the Magic Mirror to teleport you back to your bed!' 'Thank you Mirror!'
Tasks: Magic MirrorRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Red Bed
Ice Breakers
Found in Villages in Taigas or Snowy Taigas
Ice Breakers First Ability is to make your Balance as solid as a rock. Knockback is decreased and slipping on Ice is decreased as well. The Second Ability is Earthquake! While falling select Earthquake with Left Alt and when you land it will cause a shockwave beneath you damaging all mobs nearby.
Tasks: Ice BreakerRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Ice ×10
Blazing Flask
Found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions
You like Flying? You like Arson? You like both? Then the Blazing Flask is perfect for you! Right Click the Blazing Flask near Fire sources and a circle will be made around it. In the circle you will be granted Creative Flight. The circle can be made bigger through upgrading it in the Research Window and by adding more Fire!
Tasks: Blazing FlaskRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Netherrack ×10
Spore Sack
Found in Jungle Pyramids
The Spore Sack is all about.. you guessed it! Spores!!! The First Ability releases a Spore everytime you are hit. The Spore will fly around until it sticks to a Block and will explode when a mob comes near. The Second Ability allows you to accumulate Spores. Everytime you are hit 1 Spore is released and 1 is kept in your Spore Sack to be used for later. Third Ability allows floating Spores to reproduce like cells, divide and multiply! Last Ability is best of them all! Using Left Alt you can release all Spores accumulated! Their size is dependent on your health as well.
Tasks: Spore SackRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Spore Blossom ×10
Shadow Glaive
Found in End Cities and End Ships
Shadow Glaives are more Weapons than Relic. First Ability is just throwing 1 Glaive. After it hits a mob, it'll bounce back to other mobs, and maybe return back to you. You can upgrade it for more damage, bounces, and quicker recharge. The Second Ability uses all its charges to release a giant saw! It's very cool I recommend trying it out!
Tasks: Shadow GlaiveRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Roller Skates
Found in Mineshafts or Strongholds
Allows you to move much faster on all blocks by letting you accelerate while running on them! Warning much more slippery! Upgrade them to go even faster.
Tasks: Roller SkatesRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10
Infinity Ham
Found in Mineshafts or Strongholds
The Eternal Steak, oh wait wrong mod. The Infinity Ham works as an infinite food source. Eat all the Meat off the Bone and it'll Regenerate after some time. You can upgrade it to fill your belly more. The Second Ability of the Infinity Ham is marinating it in Potions. When you do that, everytime you eat from the Ham you will get that Potion Effect. If you eat all the Meat it will lose the Effect though.
Tasks: Infinite HamRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Ham ×10
Leather Belt
Found in Mineshafts or Strongholds
Holds Talismans... not much else. Might also hold your Pants up but haven't tested it yet.
Tasks: Leather BeltRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Leather ×10
Wool Mittens
Found in Villages in Taigas or Snowy Taigas
This ones very simple. Put on your Mittens, pick up some Snow, mush it together, and Boom you just made a Snowball! These are better than Vanilla Snowballs, these were made with Mittens!
Tasks: Wool MittenRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Snow Block ×5
Amphibian Boots
Found in Shipwrecks and Ocean Ruins
These little fishy boots help you to swim faster with the First Ability. Upgrade them to swim slightly faster!
Second Ability works with Water as well, just the one from the sky. You will run faster when it is raining.
The Last Ability somehow affects your lungs, you get a chance at not using Oxygen Bubbles when underwater.
Tasks: Amphibian BootRewards: Relic Experience Bottle ×10 Water Bucket
Overworld
These Relics can be found in the Overworld!
Tasks: Visit OverworldRewards: Grass Block ×32
The Nether
These Relics can be found in The Nether!
Tasks: Visit The NetherRewards: Netherrack ×32
The End
These Relics can be found in The End!
Tasks: Visit The EndRewards: End Stone ×32

entries.text:
Basic Armor
Leather Armor
7
Leather Armor is the worst Armor set you can get.
That is mostly because Mojang expected you to get it before any other.
I almost never get it though because I struggle to find that many Cows, sorry Mojang!

Chainmail Armor
12
Chainmail Armor is a little worse than Iron. Its main use in Minecraft was its elusive nature, only being obtained through Trades and Mob Drops.
Of course this is modded though, so we can craft it now! Which takes away its purpose...
Tasks: Chainmail Helmet Chainmail Chestplate Chainmail Leggings Chainmail BootsRewards: 1 XP levels

11
Golden Armor is right between Iron and Leather. But its Durability is much closer to Leather.
There is not much use for it besides having Piglins Neutral towards you when wearing some Gold Armor.

Iron Helmet

Zombies and Skeletons stand just about no chance!

20
Diamond Armor is the next on the Vanilla chain, this is also usually where we start Enchanting it as well!
I recommend Protection and its various forms, we don't have to be picky with modded!

Looking to create virtual storage using a mod like
These are great ways to upgrade your storage, but it is important to talk about
and the best way to store them.
NBT items are items with extra tags attached to them. Enchanted items, items with durability and more. These are items with NBT tags attached to them. Because of this, they don't usually stack.
When you store a lot of these into a storage system like AE2, you run the chance of creating issues for your save or server.
Because of this, it is best to store them in Chests or Bags!
The Storage Controller allows you to work with multiple storages as if they were one big storage multiblock.

This allows for a very large storage network, which can be combined with mods like Applied Energistics or Integrated Dynamics, as the Storage Controller acts as an in/out point for all storages attached to it.

Connecting either can be done by simply putting storages next to Storage Controller or next to others that are already connected to Storage Controller (this works up to 14 blocks away from controller in all directions).
The Storage Link allows you to connect multiple storages that are not attached to a Storage Controller or any blocks that are connected to it.
So its a way to wirelessly connect a "multiblock" of storages without needing to right-click each one of them.

The Storage Controller is also able to connect to other storages wirelessly, this is possible using the Storage Tool, just right click the Storage Controller to bind it and right click the storages to link them.
The range for wireless linking is the same as regular, 14 blocks of space.
Chests have 27 slots and can be made into a double chest to store twice that amount.
Trapped Chests are the same as regular Chests only the emit a Redstone signal when opened and they can't be combined together into 1.
Barrels work the same as Chests only they can't be combined together into 1. They look cool though.
Ender Chests all share the same inventory and that inventory is different for every player. They can't be combined together into 1.
Minecarts with Chests are Minecarts with Chests in them. You can't ride in these but they can be useful for transporting items across Rail systems.
Boats with Chests are Boats with Chests on them. You can open the chest while you're in the Boat or you can right-click on it. Only one person can ride in the Boat at a time.
The Copper Chest can be made but is not needed to make an Iron Chest, it can be used if you want to save some Iron though.

entries.name: Pylons

text.v: Pylons is a wonderful mod made by our very own
Don't let the size of the mod make you underestimate it! It provides many Pylons which can be used for many things to help make playing Minecraft easier.
To get started you'll need some Polished Blackstone to make them.
The Expulsion Pylon works as a way of keeping people off your lawn.
When placed down it will keep any Players who aren't whitelisted from a set amount of Chunks around it.
The Chunks are set in it's GUI in the top left from 1x1, 3x3, or 5x5 Chunks.
Also no it can't be set too close to Spawn. We know what you trolls want and we ain't giving it!
To Whitelist players check the Player Filter Quest!
This Pylon is all about blocking Mob Spawns.
You can use Mob Filters to block spawns of only certain Mobs or use the Lifeless Filter to block all Mob spawns!
You can stack multiple Mob Filters to block off more spawns. Plus you can change the Working Area for how far it blocks those Mob Spawns.
If you use the Lifeless Filter it will ignore all those settings.
Harvester Pylons work as a very simple Auto-Farm. Put the Pylon on or in the Water Source and it will automatically harvest and replant Crops that are fully grown in the set area around it.
The area can be set to 3x3, 5x5, 7x7, or 9x9 Blocks around the Pylon.
It will need a Hoe to use on the Plants and will need an Inventory like a chest above it to put the Crops. Do all that and if it's turned On it will start farming!
(Careful when using a lot of modifiers with it like Lilypads or fertilizer as when it goes very fast farming it can be a TPS eater).
The Infusion Pylon works similar as a Beacon just much better and cheaper!
When a Potion Effect is put in by a Potion Filter, it will continuously give you the Potion Effect while you're in the set Chunk area.
The Explusion Pylon pushes players out of the area, but what if you want
players nearby! Then you'll need a Player Filter.
Right Click a Player with it to set them in it, and then put it into the Pylon to Whitelist them!
So when everyone else is pushed out, your friend won't be!
Also by default the Owner of the Pylon won't get expuled.
To set the Mob Filter you just have to click the Mob you never want to see again, with the Mob Filter.
Each Filter can only hold 1 Mob so if you want Zombies, Skeletons, Spiders, Creepers, and Endermen to no longer spawn you'll need 5 Mob Filters.
You can exchange the Mob in it by simplying clicking a different Mob with it.
In order to put Potion Effects into you'll need to fill a Potion Filter.
To do so: have a Potion Effect on you, then right click with the Potion Filter to remove it from you and add it to the Filter, and repeat until it's filled and active.
This also works with modded Potion Effects or ones you can't usually get through Potions like Haste or Resistance.
The Harvester Pylon needs a Hoe to work.
(Hoes that can't break will work forever, Hoes that can will need to be replaced).
This Quest has been authored by
, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by
This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.
With the Lifeless Filter you will never have to worry about any Mob spawns within a 25x25 Block area.
That's enough to cover every distance Mobs spawn near the player. Hostile or Passive.
This includes every Y Level as well, above or below the Pylon, so no more worrying about lighting up caves!
There's no Whitelisting with this Filter, it will prevent every Mob Spawn.

Lifeless Filter
Finally peace and quiet. 
With the Lifeless Filter you will never have to worry about any Mob spawns within a 25x25 Block area.
That's enough to cover every distance Mobs spawn near the player. Hostile or Passive.
This includes every Y Level as well, above or below the Pylon, so no more worrying about lighting up caves!
There's no Whitelisting with this Filter, it will prevent every Mob Spawn.

Each individual block can then provide its own separate set of channels, so long as no single controller block is surrounded by 4 other blocks along the same plane.

An ME Network may only contain one multiblock controller at any given time. Attempting to connect more than one controller on separate parts of the network will cause a conflict, shutting down the whole network.

With the 1k Storage Component, you can now craft yourself a 1k ME Item Storage Cell to start your digital item storage system. You'll most likely want the majority of your storage to be for items, so you'll probably want to make a few

ME Item Storage Cells can each hold up to 63 different types of items. Each new type of item added to a cell will take up a certain fraction of the storage cell's total capacity in bytes. For each type already present, 1 'byte' counts for 8 items of that same type.
As an example, a 1k Item Storage Cell containing only cobblestone can hold up to 8128 cobblestone (8*1024b - 8b/type * 1 type).
If a cell is empty, it can be repurposed by disassembling it into its respective component and housing. This is done by sneaking and right-clicking in the air with the cell in your hand.
Items are not the only things that can be stored in ME cells.

Note that all storage cells, regardless of what they're designed to store, only differ in terms of their housing; both item and fluid cells use the same kind of storage component to make.

Cells can also be given a higher or lower 'priority' via the workbench, i.e. allow the cell to be the first to receive certain items until full, or made to wait for other higher-priority cells to fill up first.

entries.text:
Applied Energistics 2
Applied Energistics 2
Virtual Storage System
Welcome to Applied Energistics 2!
Applied Energistics 2 (or AE2 for short) is an incredibly versatile digital storage mod, allowing for extremely efficient storage and all sorts of automation capabilities to greatly augment your modded Minecraft experience from as early as you want to the very endgame.
For more information on AE2 beyond this chapter, consult the wiki over at appliedenergistics.github.io.
Tasks: Any ChestsRewards: 10 XP
First Things First
First Things First
Two of the very first things you will need to get started in AE2 are the Charger and the Inscriber.
The Charger, when supplied with power, will take Certus Quartz Crystals and charge them. These Charged Certus Crystals can then be used in the production of Fluix, another important resource in the mod. It can also be used to charge any item that stores power.
The Inscriber can be used to turn the various quartz crystals in AE2 into their dust form, but more importantly is used to fabricate special Printed Circuits and Processors, as will become clearer in the next quest.
Tasks: Charger InscriberRewards: Iron Ingot ×3 50 XP
Meteorite hunting
'COMIC #42: shearching 4 bobby [Fischer]'
It is time to find Meteorites that contain Sky Stone. These can be either on the surface or underground, and contain a Mysterious Cube in its center.
This cube contains all of the different Presses used in the Inscriber to make AE2's special crafting components.
The easiest way to locate a meteorite is by crafting a Meteorite Compass by placing a compass inside of a Charger.
Tasks: Meteorite Compass Advancement: ae2:main/pressesRewards: Sky Stone ×4 100 XP
Energy Acceptor
Plug in
While the Inscriber and Charger will natively accept RF/FE, the vast majority of an ME network uses its own dedicated power system called AE.
RF/FE can be converted into the native AE at a ratio of 2:1 RF:AE, either directly through an ME Controller, or through the Energy Acceptor, which can instead be connected to any part of the network.
Tasks: Energy AcceptorRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
Energy Cell
By default, an ME network on its own only has an internal buffer of 800AE without an ME Controller, with the controller adding an extra 8kAE per block. For large enough networks, this can be insufficient and may cause a network to power off intermittently when trying to recoup power for any connected devices.
The Energy Cell allows for an ME network to hold significantly more energy, adding another 200kAE per regular Energy Cell and 1.6MAE per Dense Energy Cell. These can also be placed anywhere in the network to provide the increased energy buffer.
Tasks: Energy Cell Dense Energy CellRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Energy Card
The Energy Card can be applied to most chargeable devices like Portable Cells and Wireless Terminals (covered later) to also increase their energy buffer.
Tasks: Energy CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Processors
Once you have obtained a full set of the required Inscriber Presses, it's time to start making some Processors. These are an important crafting ingredient used to make the large majority of ME-connected devices.
Tasks: Logic Processor Calculation Processor Engineering ProcessorRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Fluix
Arguably the most important resource you will need next is Fluix, used throughout the vast majority of AE2 devices and serving as a base for crafting all of the cabling within an ME network.
You'll typically want to mass produce these, and the way to do so is to make a Fluix Crystal by throwing Nether Quartz, Charged Certus quartz and Redstone together in a pool of water. This will give you a Fluix Crystal which you can turn to dust in an Inscriber.
Tasks: Fluix Dust Fluix CrystalRewards: Fluix Dust ×4 Random loot roll 100 XP
Basic Cabling
To connect the vast majority of your ME network together, you will need some cable. ME Glass Cable is the first and most basic kind of cable, and you'll be making this all throughout as the first step towards crafting the other kinds of cable.
Both glass cables and their covered counterpart can carry up to 8 channels along a single section of cabling. Unlike glass cables, covered cables can subsequently be crafted into dense covered cables, capable of carrying up to 32 channels. However, most 'multipart' devices such as buses and terminals cannot be directly attached to dense cables, requiring normal-width cables to form a connection instead.
All cables can also be crafted with dye to colour them. Uncoloured ('Fluix') cables can connect to any other colour of cable, but otherwise differently-coloured cables will never connect to one another.
Tasks: Any Glass Cable Any Covered Cable Any Covered Dense CableRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Advanced Cabling
'S.M.R.T.'
The ME Smart Cable and Dense Smart Cable function identically to the covered cables in terms of channel distribution, but will also visibly display the amount of channels they are using as coloured lines along themselves.
Tasks: Any Smart Cable Any Smart Dense CableRewards: Random loot roll Quartz Fiber ×2 50 XP
Terminals
[Linux user joke goes here]
Terminals provide access to any of the contents of an ME network. The standard ME Terminal simply lists everything in the network as one large grid to pull from and insert into, akin to a single inventory.
The ME Crafting Terminal is an extension of the ME Terminal which also provides a built-in crafting grid, allowing for convenient crafting using any item contained in the network and visible through the terminal screen.
Tasks: ME Terminal ME Crafting TerminalRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
The Storage
Items as a file system
Arguably the most important aspect of Applied Energistics 2 is its storage system, making use of digital Storage Cells. These cells are accessible through either an ME Chest for single cells, or an ME Drive for multiple cells.
The ME Chest holds a single Cell at a time, which can then be read from and written to from any other terminal on the same network. The ME Chest itself also provides its own terminal screen on the top with specific access only to the cell it contains.
The ME Drive can hold up to 10 assorted Storage Cells in the space of a single block and a single ME channel. However, it does not provide its own terminal screen, requiring some external terminal elsewhere on the network for storage access.
Tasks: ME Chest ME DriveRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
The IO
OI, OI, OI!
To make life that much easier, AE2 provides a whole suite of devices for the manipulation of ME data, i.e. moving stored items around the world.
The ME Interface is one of these devices. As an input device, the Interface allows any item/fluid/etc to be piped externally through it, which is then automatically stored in the ME Network that the interface is connected to.
As an output device, the Interface can be configured to keep a certain available amount of a stored item in stock, from the ME network to its own internal inventory. This allows items to then be received by some external source like another player or some pipe.
Tasks: Any InterfaceRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Auto-Crafting
Order up
Storage is nice and all that, but what good is a storage system if it's clogged up with raw materials needing to be crafted and processed into something and you're still stuck with having to do so manually?
AE2's auto-crafting system begins with the ME Pattern Provider. The Pattern Provider holds certain items called Patterns (covered in the next quest) which are programmed to hold some recipe that turns input items into a certain output. Up to 9 patterns can fit in one provider.
You'll often be making use of multiple pattern providers scattered all throughout your base, which is why it's useful to have a Pattern Access Terminal to remotely access the contents of any and all providers on your wider ME network.
Tasks: Any Pattern Provider ME Pattern Access TerminalRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Controller
The last piece of the puzzle for any large ME network is the ME Controller.
A controller supplies an ME Network with a far larger number of channels than the standard 8 channels for ad-hoc networks, providing 32 channels out of each face of the block for a total of 216 channels.
That's only for a single-block controller, however, since the ME Controller is in fact a multi-block structure. The controller can be up to 7x7x7 blocks in size and can come in any freeform arrangement within that maximum size. Each individual block can then provide its own separate set of channels, so long as no single controller block is surrounded by 4 other blocks along the same plane.
An ME Network may only contain one multiblock controller at any given time. Attempting to connect more than one controller on separate parts of the network will cause a conflict, shutting down the whole network.
Tasks: ME ControllerRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Quartz Wrench
Does exactly what you'd expect
The Quartz Wrench does what any regular tech mod wrench would do. It rotates blocks and devices along the face you right-click on and dismantles them when right-clicked while sneaking.
This Wrench comes in both Certus Quartz and Nether Quartz varieties.
Tasks: Any Quartz WrenchRewards: 10 XP
Network Tools
The Network Tool is an important tool throughout AE2, which is used to display various details of a network on-screen such as overall power consumption and storage.
As an added bonus, it also provides its own small inventory used to hold upgrade cards, which can be accessed when looking at any upgradeable device's screen for easy replacement. However, it cannot rotate blocks attached to the ME network like a regular wrench, only dismantle them when sneaking.
Tasks: Network ToolRewards: 50 XP
Creating your first Storage Cell
The first kilobyte.
Each individual cell has a certain capacity dictated by the component that the cell has been crafted with.
The first of the components is the 1k ME Storage Component, providing 1024 'bytes' of storage for a given cell. More on that later.
Tasks: 1k ME Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
4k Storage Component
x4
The second tier of storage component, providing 4096 bytes of storage.
Tasks: 4k ME Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
16k Storage Component
x4^2
The third tier of storage component, providing 16384 bytes of storage.
Tasks: 16k ME Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
64k Storage Component
x4^3
The fourth tier of storage component, providing 65536 bytes of storage.
Tasks: 64k ME Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
256k Storage Component
x4^4
The fifth and final AE2-standard tier of storage component, providing 262144 bytes of storage.
Tasks: 256k ME Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
1M Storage Component
The first MEGAbyte.
There comes a point in any playthrough of a large modpack where even the highest standard tier of storage cell doesn't cut it for the amount of items and resources that you may be accumulating.
This is where the MEGA Cells add-on comes in, extending the available tiers of storage into the megabyte territory. The first of these new tiers is given by the 1M MEGA Storage Component, providing 1024 kilobytes, or 1048576 bytes, of storage.
Tasks: 1M MEGA Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
4M Storage Component
x4
The second MEGA tier of storage component, providing 4194304 (4096k) bytes of storage.
Tasks: 4M MEGA Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
16M Storage Component
x4^2
The third MEGA tier of storage component, providing 16777216 (16384k) bytes of storage.
Tasks: 16M MEGA Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
64M Storage Component
x4^3
The fourth MEGA tier of storage component, providing 67108864 (65536k) bytes of storage.
Tasks: 64M MEGA Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
256M Storage Component
x4^4
The fifth and final MEGA tier of storage component, providing 268435456 (262144k) bytes of storage.
Tasks: 256M MEGA Storage ComponentRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Item Storage
With the 1k Storage Component, you can now craft yourself a 1k ME Item Storage Cell to start your digital item storage system. You'll most likely want the majority of your storage to be for items, so you'll probably want to make a few ME Item Storage Cells.
ME Item Storage Cells can each hold up to 63 different types of items. Each new type of item added to a cell will take up a certain fraction of the storage cell's total capacity in bytes. For each type already present, 1 'byte' counts for 8 items of that same type.
As an example, a 1k Item Storage Cell containing only cobblestone can hold up to 8128 cobblestone (8*1024b - 8b/type * 1 type).
If a cell is empty, it can be repurposed by disassembling it into its respective component and housing. This is done by sneaking and right-clicking in the air with the cell in your hand.
Tasks: 1k ME Item Storage CellRewards: Random loot roll ME Item Cell Housing 100 XP
Smart Filter
Items are not the only things that can be stored in ME cells. ME Fluid Storage Cells can store liquids such as water, lava and any variety of modded oils and fuels, just to give a few examples.
Note that all storage cells, regardless of what they're designed to store, only differ in terms of their housing; both item and fluid cells use the same kind of storage component to make.
For fluids, 1 byte equals 8 buckets (8000mb).
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Cell Workbench
The Cell Workbench allows for cells to be 'partitioned' to hold specific items, i.e. given a whitelist filter. It also allows the cell to be upgraded with certain upgrade cards such as the Inverter Card, which sets the aforementioned whitelist to be a blacklist instead.
Cells can also be given a higher or lower 'priority' via the workbench, i.e. allow the cell to be the first to receive certain items until full, or made to wait for other higher-priority cells to fill up first.
Tasks: Cell WorkbenchRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME IO Port
Defragmentation
The ME IO Port allows for the contents of an ME network's storage to be quickly rearranged between different storage media such as ME cells and external containers connected to storage buses.
When a cell is inserted in an input slot on the left, the IO Port can be toggled to either empty the cell out into other ME storages or fill the (ideally, partitioned) cell with certain items spread out across other storages.
Tasks: ME IO PortRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
ME Import Bus
The I
The ME Import Bus periodically sucks items in from whatever external storage the bus is facing. It can optionally be filtered to only take in certain items from said inventory.
Tasks: ME Import BusRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Export Bus
The O
The ME Export Bus periodically spits items in its whitelist filter out to whatever external storage the bus is facing. Unlike the Import Bus, the Export Bus cannot work without being filtered.
Tasks: ME Export BusRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Annihilation Plane
GET IN
The ME Annihilation Plane can be used to automatically break any blocks in front of it and return anything dropped by the block directly to the ME network.
As an added bonus, the Annihilation Plane can be enchanted in the same way as a regular digging tool, affecting block drops in the same way as that enchanted tool would. This makes it ideal for processing ore blocks when enchanted with Fortune, for example. Any added enchantments significantly increase the amount of energy used by the plane every time a block is broken. Enchanting the plane with Efficiency will decrease the overall energy use incurred by all other enchantments, while the Unbreaking enchantment gives the plane the chance to only use any energy sometimes, similarly to Unbreaking on regular tools.
Tasks: ME Annihilation PlaneRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Formation Plane
GET OUT
The ME Formation Plane acts similarly to the Storage Bus, but treats the world itself as its storage medium. In other words, it will place down any block in its filter directly in front of itself.
This can be useful for situations where a block can be processed simply by placing it and breaking it with a certain tool.
Tasks: ME Formation PlaneRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
P2P Tunnels
Cut out the middleman
P2P (peer-to-peer) is a powerful system within AE2, allowing for the transfer of items, fluids and even more without the need for any intermediary ME storage.
Right-clicking on a P2P tunnel with certain items will attune the tunnel into one capable of transferring something else, such as items through pipes, energy through cables, redstone signals and (by default) even ME connections themselves.
P2P tunnels must be linked to one another with the use of a Memory Card, detailed in the next quest.
Tasks: ME P2P TunnelRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Storage Bus
The spare chest
The ME Storage Bus, when facing some external storage container, will allow the container to be used as though it were part of the ME network, allowing items to be taken out from the container or inserted into it purely via ME.
Storage buses can be filtered and given specific priorities such that specific items will try to go to the attached storage first, however it will not retroactively move any filtered items from anywhere else in the network to its attached storage.
Tasks: ME Storage BusRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Memory Card
The Memory Card is a tool with two different functions. The simplest of the two is to save various devices' configurations (such as whitelist filters) to be copied over to another device of the same kind.
The second function of a memory card is to link P2P tunnels together. When doing so, the P2P tunnel being linked will be assigned a unique ID, which is stored on the memory card for further linking.
Tasks: Memory CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Equal Distribution Card
ME Storage &mCells&r Drawers
The Equal Distribution Card is an upgrade for storage cells that pre-allocates a certain amount of items that can be taken up by any individual type.
This behaviour is comparable to something like a Functional Storage drawer, wherein each compartment holds a set number of stacks as opposed to allowing items from one compartment to leak into the others and crowd other kinds of items out.
Tasks: Equal Distribution CardRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
Overflow Destruction Card
This behaviour is comparable to something like a Functional Storage drawer, wherein each compartment holds a set number of stacks as opposed to allowing items from one compartment to leak into the others and crowd other kinds of items out.
Tasks: Overflow Destruction CardRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
Smart Filter
Portable Cells function identically to regular cells in that they can be inserted into a chest or drive and filled accordingly.
However, unlike regular cells, their contents can also be accessed standalone via the cell item itself, a bit like a digital ME-flavoured backpack.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Capacity Card
The Capacity Card allows a bus upgraded with it to carry a larger filter. Import and Export buses upgraded with capacity cards can go from supporting only one filtered item each to their maximum nine-slot filter, while Storage buses will go from 18 slots to a maximum of 63.
Tasks: Capacity CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Forgot to Mention
This has a use outside of crafting cables.
An important concept within AE2 is a technique known as 'subnetting', wherein an extra separate ME network (a subnetwork) acts in conjunction with the main network to perform some specialised function or process.
What separates a subnetwork from a completely detached separate network is usually the use of the Quartz Fiber as a cable part. When placed between two otherwise unconnected lengths of cable, the Quartz Fiber transfers no data or channels between the two whatsoever, instead only transmitting power.
Thus, a subnetwork on the other side of the Fiber can be powered wholly by the main network's power source, without requiring any extra dedicated powergen.
Tasks: Quartz FiberRewards: Random loot roll 10 XP
Patterns
Patterns are what hold an encoded recipe to be fulfilled by a Pattern Provider. To encode a recipe onto a Pattern, the ME Pattern Encoding Terminal must be used.
Patterns can be set to hold either a regular crafting recipe, which will require the use of a Molecular Assembler on the face of its Provider, or a more general 'processing' recipe, wherein any input items can be sent out by the provider into some other machine block or specialised processing plant.
Tasks: ME Pattern Encoding Terminal Blank PatternRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Molecular Assembler
The Molecular Assembler is AE2's equivalent of an automatic crafting table, required to fulfil any and all crafting pattern jobs.
Molecular Assemblers are capable of transferring power and channels to other ME devices connected to it, but will not themselves take up a channel. Up to 6 MAs can be connected to a single Pattern Provider (if employed) to allow for more crafts to be done in parallel.
MAs also each have their own dedicated slot for a single crafting pattern, allowing them to function standalone when powered. When operated in this way, any matching items inserted into the MA will be automatically crafted into the result of the pattern.
Tasks: Molecular AssemblerRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
ME Level Emitter
The ME Level Emitter, when configured with a specific item and quantity of it to respond to, will emit a redstone signal depending on whether that item stored in the network either falls below, goes above or equals the given quantity.
This can be used, for example, to automatically switch certain machines on with redstone to auto-craft a resource when it falls below a given minimum amount.
Tasks: ME Level EmitterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Redstone-Controlled ME
Individual ME devices can also be configured to respond to redstone signals. When upgraded with a Redstone Card, a device can be configured to do work only when powered with redstone or otherwise as needed.
This behavior can also apply to entire sections of an ME network by using an ME Toggle Bus. This allows a section of the network on the other side of the bus to come online only when the bus is powered by redstone, or to go offline if using an inverted toggle bus.
Tasks: Redstone Card ME Toggle BusRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Crafting Card
Automation in upgrade form!
When applied as an upgrade to any supported device such as an Interface or Export Bus, the Crafting Card allows the device in question to automatically send out its own crafting requests for a required (filtered) item. Crafting CPUs can be set to respond only to these requests to prevent taking up CPUs meant for player-requested crafts.
When the Level Emitter is upgraded with the Crafting Card, it can be configured to emit redstone in order to directly facilitate in crafting, by emitting a signal either while a crafting job for its given item is detected or specifically to craft the item. The latter would apply for cases where the only thing needed to make a given item is a redstone signal, without even requiring a crafting pattern.
Tasks: Crafting CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Growth Accelerator
Naturally, AE2 provides its own way to dramatically speed up crystal growth.
Place these around your Budding Crystals, give them some power, and watch your crystals grow!
Tasks: Growth AcceleratorRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Acceleration Card
The Acceleration Card, depending on the device being upgraded with it, will either increase the speed at which the device operates or allow the device to carry out more operations in one go.
In the case of the Molecular Assembler, a full set of 5 cards reduces the time taken for the MA to fulfil a craft from one second (with no cards) to one tick.
Tasks: Acceleration CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Spatial IO
Aside from the storage of items and fluids, AE2 also provides a native way of storing entire structures inside of storage cells, not too dissimilarly to the Compact Machines mod.
The Spatial IO Port allows structures contained within a Spatial Containment Structure to be captured within a specially-designed storage cell, activated via a redstone signal.
If a mob or player happens to stand inside of the SCS while the space is being captured, they too will be transported to where the rest of the space goes, i.e. in a dedicated dimension. Just make sure you have a way to get back out and in if you're the one being captured.
Tasks: Spatial IO PortRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Spatial Pylon
The Spatial Containment Structure (SCS) consists of a cage of Spatial Pylons covering the volume you wish to enclose in a Spatial IO cell. At the absolute minimum, an SCS requires three lines of spatial pylon blocks, one for each dimension of the space being contained (length, width, height).
However, Spatial IO is an extremely power-hungry feature, especially when trying to capture much larger spaces (up to 128x128x128). Having more spatial pylons included in the SCS around the desired volume will increase its overall efficiency, allowing it to use less energy to capture.
Also, be mindful that each individual pylon (regardless of its length) takes up one channel. For particularly large spaces, you may wish to build a dedicated network with a controller to fit all the required pylons.
Tasks: Spatial PylonRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Spatial Anchor
The Spatial Anchor is a companion device from the Spatial IO lineage that simply functions as a chunk loader. When connected to an ME network, the Anchor will force-load all the chunks occupied by the ME network across all cables and devices, excluding subnetworks, as long as the network remains powered.
Tasks: Spatial AnchorRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Spatial Storage Cell
Spatial Storage Cells are used to hold one defined volume each, and come in three different capacities allowing for a maximum of 2x2x2, 16x16x16 and 128x128x128 blocks' worth of space.
Upon encoding, a cell is allocated a section of space within the spatial storage dimension, along with a unique ID corresponding to the region allocated to the cell. An encoded cell can still be used within the Spatial IO Port to retrieve any stored blocks and entities.
From then on, any blocks contained either within the cell's region of space or in an SCS with the same size as the one used for the initial encoding can be moved back into the overworld or into the spatial dimension respectively. If there are blocks both within the spatial region and within the SCS, these will simply swap places accordingly.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Smart Filter
Download more RAM
Before you can carry out an auto-crafting job, you need a device to actually store the request itself along with any interim items for multi-step crafts. This device is known as a crafting CPU.
A crafting CPU is a multiblock structure requiring at least one Crafting Storage block, optionally along with any other Crafting Unit. The multiblock can be made in any size, but must be a solid cuboid in order to form and function accordingly.
Tasks: Smart FilterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Crafting Co-Processing Unit
Download more CPU cores
The Crafting Co-Processing Unit helps speed up crafting jobs by allowing pattern providers to either send items out to their connected devices faster or to work concurrently to make multiple required ingredients.
The base AE2 co-processor provides one co-processor 'thread' to assist this, while the co-processing unit from MEGA Cells provides 4 threads in a single such block.
Tasks: Crafting Co-Processing UnitRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Crafting Monitor
Download more VRAM
The Crafting Monitor displays the overall item being crafted, along with the remaining quantity of that item still being crafted.
Both the base AE2 monitor and the MEGA monitor function identically, but are provided for aesthetic purposes.
Tasks: Crafting MonitorRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Cable Anchor
Under the knife
The Quartz Cutting Knife, like the wrench, comes in both nether and certus quartz flavours and is a useful crafting tool to have on hand.
Cables can also be separated without needing to be coloured by attaching a Cable Anchor between them, crafted using this knife and craftable up to 50 times with the same knife before it breaks.
Cable Anchors can also be used to craft Cable Facades, allowing you to disguise cables within walls by covering them with the face of an arbitrary block. While facade recipes are hidden in JEI, you can still craft them by taking any regular block and surrounding it with 4 cable anchors in the crafting grid.
Aside from crafting anchors, the cutting knife also has another use: right-clicking with the knife will open a small GUI that allows you to craft Inscriber Name Presses. When given a name, these presses can be used inside of an Inscriber to rename any input item with the name of the press. Two of these presses can be concatenated in the inscriber to rename the item to the name of the top press, followed by the bottom one.
Tasks: Any Knife Cable Anchor Inscriber Name PressRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
Color Applicator
The Color Applicator is a chargeable tool that allows for in-world dyeing of cables. It functions more or less as a specialised storage cell to be loaded up with either vanilla dyes or paint balls for specific colours, along with snowballs to wash colours off and turn cables back to their Fluix variant.
Applying colour to a cable uses 100AE of energy from its internal battery, for a total of 3400 cable segments in a single charge.
Tasks: Color ApplicatorRewards: Random loot roll 50 XP
The... Weapons?
Too hot for the ATF
These last three items are more or less some extra toys provided by AE2 and don't necessarily fit under any of these quest trees.
The Charged Staff is just a simple powered staff which deals 3 hearts of damage and consumes 300AE per hit. It also uses pre-1.9 combat mechanics, meaning that you can spam-click with this like in the good old days.
The Entropy Manipulator, when used on certain blocks in the world, will smelt them in-place, such as sand to glass and metal ores to metal ingots. If not, it will simply light a fire on the block.
Finally, the Matter Cannon functions similarly to the Color Applicator as a dedicated cell for holding 'ammo' items such as Matter Balls and iron/gold nuggets, which can then be fired out to deal damage to mobs or break blocks. Heavier 'ammo'Matter Balls in a Matter Cannon can be substituted with Paint Balls, which will apply a paint splatter effect on the face of whatever block being fired at. Lumen Paint Balls are a variant of paint balls exclusively used by the Matter Cannon, whose paint splatters also give off some light once present in the world.
Tasks: Charged Staff Entropy Manipulator Matter CannonRewards: Random loot roll 10 XP
ME Wireless Access Point
The next thing to make to allow for wireless network access is the ME Wireless Access Point. The Access Point is used to open the network to wireless access via a wireless terminal, and has a set (finite) range depending on how many Wireless Boosters are inserted into the access point.
Tasks: ME Wireless Access Point Wireless BoosterRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Condensed Matter
As for wirelessly expanding the ME Network itself, the first step is admittedly somewhat unorthodox.
The Matter Condenser is AE2's take on a trash can, voiding any items inserted into it. When fitted with a Storage Component, however, the condenser can harness some left-over energy from the item being voided and store it to make two special crafting items out of enough concentrated energy.
The first of these two items is the Matter Ball, requiring at least a 1k storage component and 256 items' worth of voided material.
Tasks: Matter Condenser Matter BallRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Wireless Terminals
This is what you're here for
The Wireless Terminal functions identically to a regular terminal, but wirelessly.
Before it can be used to access a network, it must first be linked to the network by placing it into the top-right slot of the Wireless Access Point. If it is not linked to a network, or is out of either range or power, the terminal will not function.
Wireless terminals can also be upgraded with Energy Cards to provide a larger internal battery.
Tasks: Wireless Terminal Wireless Crafting TerminalRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Infinity Booster
I'm not writing the Toy Story line
The AEInfinityBooster add-on provides two bespoke wireless boosters allowing for infinite connectivity range, with optional cross-dimensional support.
Tasks: Infinity Range Booster Dimension CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Hyper-Condensed Matter
Hyper-Condensed Matter
When using a 64k storage component or higher, the Matter Condenser becomes able to condense significantly more to produce a Singularity. A single singularity requires 256000 items to be voided. That's exactly 4000 stacks!
See what happens when you throw this singularity on the ground with a piece of Ender Dust. You'll have to deal some damage to the surroundings while you're at it, but thankfully AE2 offers its own Tiny TNT to minimise that.
Tasks: Singularity Ender Dust Tiny TNTRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Loosely Speaking
The remaining two IO cards
The Fuzzy Card allows a filtered item to be matched regardless of any (NBT) metadata such as damage or enchantments, while the Inverter Card toggles the filter on such buses from being a whitelist to being a blacklist.
Tasks: Fuzzy Card Inverter CardRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Quantum Network Bridge
If you did that last quest correctly, you should have turned that singularity into a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities. These new singularities are used to link together a ring-shaped device known as a Quantum Network Bridge.
When two of these individual rings have been linked using the Quantum Entangled Singularities and jumpstarted with some AE power (e.g. an energy cell), an ME network can be expanded wirelessly on the other side of the bridge, across either long distances or even dimensions.
Tasks: ME Quantum Ring ×16 ME Quantum Link Chamber ×2 Quantum Entangled Singularity ×2Rewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Quest
In Applied Energistics 2, every ME network has a certain number of channels available, which simply means how many networked devices can fit on the whole network.
As a rule of thumb, any device that more or less handles ME data directly (items stored within the network) and carries out some form of I/O will take up a channel. Usually components that are only concerned with the internal power storage of the network, like Energy Cells and Inscribers, do not take up channels.
Networks without an ME Controller are known as 'ad-hoc' networks and only support a maximum of 8 channels.
Tasks: Manual check-offRewards: 10 XP
Bulk Item Storage
Bulk and cut
MEGA Cells offers the bespoke Bulk Item Storage Cell, which is limited to no more than one type of item storeable per cell but can store a practically INFINITE* number of that item type. Before it can accept an item type, it must be filtered in advance using a Cell Workbench.
*Technically "max long". If you know, you know.
Tasks: MEGA Bulk Item Storage CellRewards: Random loot roll 100 XP
Quantum Bridge Card
The Quantum Bridge Card is an alternate method to get wireless interdimensional access to your Applied Energistics system. You will need a Quantum Bridge connected at your base and a Quantum Bridge Card in your terminal. These tunnels are then bound together with a Quantum Entangled Singularity to gain access wherever you go.
Tasks: Quantum Bridge CardRewards: Random loot roll 250 XP
